evidence: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:161-167: the async goroutine calls d.Legacy.DeleteCollection, but line 166 records the result with d.recordStorageDuration(..., startLegacy). In the other async legacy paths (lines 56, 113, 140) the call is recordLegacyDuration. metrics.go:54-62 shows the two functions write to different histograms (m.legacy vs m.storage), so legacy latency gets attributed to unified storage.

go.work.sum:404 and go.work.sum:408 hold the same line, 'github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/apimachinery v0.0.0-20240701135906-559738ce6ae1/go.mod h1:DkxMin...'. The PR diff adds line 408 even though 404 already exists. It is harmless at runtime, but it is a merge artifact and `go work sync` would drop it. Low-priority cleanup.

dualwriter_mode3.go:42,55: Storage.Create returns `created`, but the goroutine passes the original `obj` to Legacy.Create. The code before the PR also passed obj, and legacy stores assign their own IDs and resource versions, so the two stores were never going to share a resourceVersion. The real risk is different: obj may already have been changed in place by Storage.Create, and the goroutine reads it concurrently with the caller using the returned object. The sibling modes handle this explicitly: mode1 uses created.DeepCopyObject() plus enrichLegacyObject (dualwriter_mode1.go:51-57), and mode2 passes the enriched result (dualwriter_mode2.go:53-58). The concern has some merit, but 'resourceVersion inconsistency' overstates it.

dualwriter_mode3.go:108-114: the goroutine runs context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...), and ctx is the request context (line 97). A child context is cancelled when its parent is cancelled, and net/http cancels the request context once the handler returns. Delete returns right after starting the goroutine (line 116), so the legacy delete can fail with context canceled. The fix is context.WithoutCancel(ctx), Go 1.21+, before adding the timeout. Same root cause as #4 and #7.

dualwriter_mode3.go:134-143: the async Legacy.Update uses a context derived from the request ctx (line 135), and Update returns right away at line 143. When the request ends, the parent context is cancelled and the legacy update can be aborted. Same root cause as #3 and #7; fix with context.WithoutCancel.

dualwriter_mode3.go:126 and :139: the same objInfo goes to Storage.Update and then to Legacy.Update, so each store calls UpdatedObject against its own current object. For patches, or for objects whose metadata or resourceVersion differs between stores, the two results can differ or fail on preconditions. Mode2 avoids this by computing `updated` once and wrapping it in updateWrapper (dualwriter_mode2.go:291,298), and mode1 does the same for its secondary write (dualwriter_mode1.go:238-250). The divergence risk is real. Severity is moderate because the legacy write here is best-effort.

dualwriter_mode3.go:42-46: when Storage.Create fails, line 45 calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage). Legacy was never called. This should be recordStorageDuration, like the success path at line 48 and the error paths in Delete and DeleteCollection (lines 103, 156).

dualwriter_mode3.go:50-57: the async Legacy.Create uses context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...), where ctx comes from the request (lines 36, 39). Create returns at line 59 without waiting. Cancelling the request context, which net/http does once the handler returns, cancels the derived context, so the safety-net legacy write may never finish. Use context.WithoutCancel(ctx) before applying the timeout.

dualwriter_mode3.go:96-97: Delete builds `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", ..., "kind", ..., "method", ...)` but then calls klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) instead of passing `log`. Every other method passes the enriched logger (lines 39, 66, 82, 123, 150), so downstream klog.FromContext calls in Delete lose the name, kind, and method fields.

dualwriter_mode3.go:106: d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage) passes the object `name` as the kind label. The error path at line 103 and the legacy path at line 113 pass options.Kind. metrics.go:59-61 uses this argument as a Prometheus label value, so object names leak into the label, raising cardinality and splitting delete metrics away from the rest.

dualwriter_mode3.go:126-130: when Storage.Update fails, line 129 calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage), but only unified storage was called. It should be recordStorageDuration, like the success path at line 132. Same copy-paste bug as #6.
